eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from global models including the ECMWF and GFS show a tight consensus for maximum temperatures in Tel Aviv on May 20 centering on 25°C, which holds the market’s leading 47% implied probability. Stable subtropical high pressure, clear skies, and light easterly flow are expected to limit afternoon heating while moderating the diurnal range in this late-spring period. Eastern Mediterranean sea surface temperatures near seasonal norms and the absence of strong upper-level support for warming further anchor the outlook around 25–26°C. The Israel Meteorological Service’s next high-resolution update, along with any late adjustments to boundary-layer mixing, could shift the narrow 24–26°C window and influence trader positioning before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from Taiwan's Central Weather Administration and international models point to a daytime high in Taipei around 33–34°C on May 20, driven by a strengthening subtropical ridge and southerly flow that limits cloud cover while boosting solar heating and humidity. These conditions typically produce peak readings near the upper end of the normal late-May range of 29–32°C, yet variable afternoon convection and possible sea-breeze effects introduce uncertainty that keeps the market-implied probabilities for 32°C, 33°C, and 34°C tightly clustered near 25 percent each. Historical climatology shows May maxima in Taipei exceed 33°C on roughly one-third of days when similar synoptic patterns occur, underscoring why traders view outcomes above 35°C as less likely without stronger ridging. Updated model runs tomorrow morning will refine the exact peak and help resolve the narrow spread among these leading outcomes.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from European and global models point to a mild spring day in Istanbul shaped by a weak frontal system bringing scattered showers and reduced sunshine, keeping daytime maxima likely between 18–20°C. This aligns with climatological norms for late May while reflecting short-term atmospheric instability that has nudged trader sentiment toward the tightly bunched 18°C and 19°C outcomes. Key variables include the precise timing of cloud cover and any last-minute strengthening of onshore flow from the Sea of Marmara, both of which can shift the peak reading by 1–2°C. Updated runs from the Turkish State Meteorological Service and ECMWF later today will provide the final guidance ahead of the 21 May resolution window.
